situations.title: Sold. Mumbai.
body: Auction night. Your name on TV, MI’s paddle up, hammer drops — SOLD. The house is crying, your phone is exploding.
This night comes once. Who gets it — home, or the world?
situations.q: What do you do right after the auction?

reader.text: Auction night. The whole family's glued to the TV, and on the screen — your name: {name}. Base price — ₹30 lakh. MI, your dream franchise, raises the paddle. Then RCB. MI again. Hammer drops — and SOLD.
Mumbai Indians. At 16. Mom's crying happy tears, Dad's hand is shaking — and your phone has fully lost it. 200 notifications. 11 missed calls from your bestie, Maddy.
Celebrate, beta — celebrate properly. But remember: MI bought you. Cricket hasn't accepted you yet. You'll have to earn that — still day 1.
This night comes once in a lifetime. Who gets it — your family, or the world?

choices.s: The internet will still be there tomorrow. This living room won't feel like this again.

dm.text: I called 11 times and you were with your family. Fair enough, bro. I'm happy, jealous, and kinda emotional too 😭
Your mom was crying, right? Now you're gonna make me cry on video call too.
Tomorrow I want the full story. Ball-by-ball. From the paddle going up to the hammer drop.

choices.s: Your name's trending right now. The moment's hot — tell the world you've arrived.
choices.postWhy: Right this second, your name is in India's trends — in an hour it'll be someone else. If the jersey post goes up now, the whole country sees it. This window won't open twice.

post.caption: First time I held the MI jersey, I didn't know whether to smile or cry. From academy nets to this blue. The dream begins tonight. 💙 #SoldToMumbai

B.caption: Bro got SOLD and had a caption ready in 4 minutes?? The superstar era is officially scary 😭

situations.title: Bumrah's Over
body: First day in the Wankhede nets — Mahela says one line: "Kid, next net. Jasprit, one over." 3 balls, beaten 3 times. The whole room is watching.
3 balls left. Student or show-off?
situations.q: How do you play Bumrah's next ball?

reader.text: First day in the Wankhede nets. You're strapping on your pads when Mahela says, without even looking up — "Kid, next net. Jasprit, one over." The whole room has shown up to watch.
Emotional post at night, straight to Bumrah in the morning. The scheduling sense of humor is savage 😄

3 balls, beaten 3 times. The length looks like one thing, passes like another. Third one — slower ball: your shot finishes before the ball even gets there. Hardik's standing there with his arms folded. Rohit's completely still.
You're guessing the length. Pick the wrist first.
3 balls left. The whole room is watching — student or show-off?

choices.t: Defend — and ask what you missed
choices.s: Getting beaten in public is embarrassing. But the information is right there.

dm.text: Good that you asked. Most don’t.

On the slower one, you're tracking the ball. Wrong thing. Track the release point — the wrist drops a beat late, fingers on the side of the ball. You get that half-second earlier. That half-second is yours.
Nets tomorrow, 7 a.m. Just slower ones. Be there.

choices.t: Charge him — make a statement shot
choices.s: The whole room is watching. So give them something worth watching.

situations.title: First Press Conference
body: First official press conference — 11 mics, sponsor board, Naman Dhir right next to you: same age, same lane, only one spot in the XI.
The first question lands straight on your chest: "Do you deserve a place in MI’s XI this season?" Whatever you say becomes a clip.
situations.q: The camera's on. What do you say?

reader.text: MI media room. Ring lights, sponsor boards, 11 mics — and a placard with your name in the middle. First press conference of your life.
Next to you: Naman Dhir. Same age, same middle-order lane. 2 names, 1 spot in the XI.
Nervous? I was too. Free advice — don’t become the headline.
In the front row, a reporter’s phone is playing your clip. The question’s been loaded since last night.
First question, straight to the chest: "16 years old. Sold for crores. Do you deserve a spot in MI’s XI?"
The next 30 seconds will become clips. You write the headline — or the headline writes you?

choices.s: "I’m here to learn. Whatever role the team gives me, I’ll do it." Boring, but bulletproof.

dm.text: Saw the presser. Good. No headline.
Let the bat make noise, keep it straight on the mic — that’s how we do it. We’ll talk role soon. Be ready.

choices.s: "I came for the XI, not to wait around." If confidence is the product, sell it.

situations.title: Hardik’s Question
body: After the meeting, Hardik signals you to stay. Mahela at the table, sheet in front of him. "Your first shot won’t be opening. No.5, maybe No.6. Maybe just 28 off 15. You ready?"
You’ve played top order your whole life. The captain isn’t listening for an answer — he’s listening to how you answer.
situations.q: What do you say to Hardik?

reader.text: Team hotel, 9:30 p.m. No playing XI on the whiteboard—just matchups: left-arm spin, death overs, powerplay, impact sub. Names come later here. Job comes first.
Meeting's over. Hardik signals: {name}, stay. Mahela opens a sheet on the table in front of you. This isn't casual.
You gave them the headline in the presser. Now I'm asking—who's the player behind the headline?
Your first shot won't be at the top—like it's always been. No. 5, maybe No. 6. Maybe just 28 off 15—not a fifty, not a highlight reel. You ready for that?
You've batted top order your whole life. The captain doesn't want an answer—he wants to know your mindset.

choices.t: Accept the role — "Wherever you want me, that's where I'll play."
choices.s: If MI needs a role, give them the role. That's where a captain's trust gets built.

dm.text: Good answer. Wasn't vague.
When the chance comes, I need flexibility—not explanations. Keep the role clear, keep your head cool.

choices.t: Ask to open — make your case
choices.s: You know your game. If you won't say it, who will?

situations.title: Team Sheet
body: 9:04 a.m. — team sheet at the door. Your name at No. 5. Wankhede tonight. IPL debut at 16.
Below that: 12th man — Naman Dhir. He’s in the corridor, and he still hasn’t seen the sheet.
situations.q: Who's gonna tell Naman—you, or the sheet?

reader.text: 9:04 a.m. Team sheet at the door. You don't have to search for your name—it's there. No. 5: {name}. 16 years old. Tomorrow night. Wankhede. IPL debut.
Your name made the sheet, and now sleep's gone 😄 Welcome to the best insomnia in the world, champ.
Below that: 12th man — Naman Dhir. He's in the corridor, on his phone—hasn't seen the sheet yet. You've got a draft ready in your phone. He's got nothing.
"Slot 1 is mine. My game will do the talking." — remember his post? You got the slot. Now there's just a 12-step corridor left.
Debut in 24 hours, and your first decision isn't with the bat—it's about the guy who wanted your spot. Who's telling him—you, or the sheet?

choices.t: Go tell him yourself — straight up, eye to eye
choices.s: He deserves to hear it from you, not a notification.

dm.text: You came to tell me yourself. Before the sheet went up.
I'm jealous, obviously. But I'll remember this. However many overs you get tomorrow night, I'll still be the one bringing drinks—now go win us the match. 🏏

choices.s: This moment is yours. The world should know right now.
choices.postWhy: The team sheet is still on the door — the world doesn’t know yet. Will the first post be yours, or some leak’s? You only get one debut announcement in a lifetime.

post.caption: DEBUT LOADING. 🔒🏏 Tomorrow night. Wankhede. Blue jersey, my number. The dream finally has a date. 💙

reader.text: 9:04 a.m. The sheet still isn’t up — you’ve been called to the selection table. In front of Mahela: a printout of your nets numbers from the week.
The numbers are honest — borderline. This week, your name maybe doesn’t make the sheet. That’s what the paper says.
I’ve read the numbers too. He still plays. My call, my responsibility.
Silence. Mahela holds the stare a beat longer — then the pen moves. No.5 — {name}. The ink is still wet.
The captain just put his name behind yours — tomorrow, your debut and his judgment both walk out to bat. How do you answer that?

choices.s: This stays in the room, not on the internet.

dm.text: You came. Good.
Listen — this isn’t charity. I saw what the sheet doesn’t. Tomorrow, show them. And this stays between us.

choices.s: The captain showed faith — the world should see it.
choices.postWhy: The captain bet on you against the numbers. If the thank-you post goes out now, the whole Paltan will see it — but what happened in the selection room goes public too.

post.caption: When the numbers didn’t speak, the captain did. @hardikpandya93 — tomorrow night is for this faith. 🙏💙 #Debut

variants.title: Orange Bib
variants.q: Day one on the bench — how do you win it?

reader.text: 9:04 a.m. The sheet’s on the door. You read it 3 times — your name isn’t there. No.5: Naman Dhir. You’re not even 12th man — orange bib, drinks duty.

Tomorrow you'll be looking at the Wankhede lights from beyond the rope — that first sheet hits hardest when your name's not on it. I spent 2 years in a bib. The way back runs through the ground, not the timeline.
Phone buzzes. Paltan Pulse just posted: "WHERE IS THE KID?? MI buys a prodigy and BENCHES him?? #JusticeFor{name}" — 8k likes and climbing.
"I came for the XI, not to wait" — the clip's doing the rounds again today. New caption: "Saw the XI. From the bench."
There are 2 roads from the bench — 1 through the ground, 1 through the timeline. Only 1 gets you back to the XI: which one are you taking?

choices.s: Drinks, throwdowns, boundary drills — the room notices who stays locked in and who sulks.

dm.text: Saw you in drills today. Bib on, still fully switched on. You were even giving Naman throwdowns.
One thing you should know — Hardik watches the bench most when he thinks no one's looking. Today, he looked. The road back starts here. 🤝

situations.title: Debut Morning
body: Debut day. You woke up 2 minutes before the alarm, kit bag packed since last night, 61 unread on your phone — everyone saying the same thing: today’s the day.
Team bus at 9. Coach Sir’s text from last night: 'Shadow practice. 20 minutes. Don’t bring your phone.'
situations.q: Where do the 3 hours before your debut go?

reader.text: 6:58 a.m., eyes open 2 minutes before the alarm. Marine Drive is half asleep — and tonight your name's on the team sheet.
Nervous? Good. Means you get what today is.
That presser headline? Tonight the ball reads that. Answer with the bat.
61 unread on your phone — all of Mumbai is saying your name. Coach's message: 'Shadow practice. 20 minutes. Don't bring your phone.'
The 3 hours before your debut are yours alone. Who do you give them to — the game, or the name?

choices.t: Lock into the routine — phone off, shadow practice
choices.s: Coach's 20-minute ritual. Game first, noise later.

dm.text: Don't send me the video, beta. I know you did it. I can tell from the sound.
Today, just three jobs: watch the first ball. Watch the second ball. Watch the third ball. Wankhede will handle the rest.
And when they announce your name—pause for a second and really hear it. That second never comes twice.

choices.t: Open your timeline — soak in the hype
choices.s: All of Mumbai is saying your name. At least hear it once.

variants.q: What are you on Naman's debut day?

reader.text: 7 a.m. Team sheet pinned — 11 names, not yours. 12th man: drinks, towels, throw-downs.
The name in your spot: Naman Dhir. The debut cap tonight goes to him — the same cap you dreamed about.
Bro… I don't even know what to say. This was my dream too. Just never thought it'd come true in front of you.
How a player looks on the bench — people notice that before they notice the XI. Everyone's watching. All the time.
There's guilt in Naman's voice, and something else in your gut. Today is his day — what do you do with yours?

choices.s: His debut, your hand. The room remembers this.

dm.text: Bro. You gave me throw-downs for forty minutes. For my debut. In the spot that should've been yours.

situations.title: First Ball
body: Wankhede packed. Chasing 178, MI are 39/2 — and you're heading down the steps with one line from Mahela in your ear: 'No. 5. Play your game.'
Up front: Noor Ahmad's wrist spin. At the death: Pathirana waiting. Your first IPL ball is about to leave your hand.
situations.q: How do you build this knock?

reader.text: Wankhede packed. CSK put up 178, MI 39/2 — Rohit gone, Tilak gone. Mahela has one line: 'No.5. Play your game.' 139 needed off 84.
Only you know this: you're in this XI because the captain insisted. Tonight, his name's on the line too.
Forget the scoreboard. Go over by over. I'll meet you at the other end.
No.5 — the role the captain gave you, and you said yes to. You know what the job is here.
Noor Ahmad's googly in front of you, Pathirana at the death, long-on and deep midwicket back. Your first IPL ball is coming — how do you play it?

choices.t: Build the chase — find the gaps, run twos, then cash in with boundaries
choices.s: The moment's big. The ball isn't. One at a time.

pass.title: 47 OFF 29
pass.note: Form beat the nerves. He played Noor's googly for ones and twos, then picked Pathirana's slower ball right out of the hand — release point, exactly the way he'd been taught. 19 off his last 2 overs. MI won, and Wankhede remembered the name.

reactions.text: I asked about the role once. Got the answer today.
Tempo. That's the word. Zero panic.

reactions.name: cricketroom_india

You read the slower ball from the hand, not the pitch. Nets tomorrow, 7 a.m. I'll be there.

choices.t: Counter-attack — make the statement from ball one
choices.s: Wankhede should remember you were here.

pass.title: 38 OFF 16
pass.note: The timing was there, so the madness turned into a plan. Noor's googly got lofted inside-out — a total SKY kind of shot. 38 (16), the stadium on its feet, and the commentary box had to ask how to spell the name.

variants.title: From the Dugout
variants.q: When the captain scans the dugout — what are you doing?

reader.text: Wankhede packed. You’re in the orange bib, drinks tray in hand. Naman’s padded up at No.6 — his first night.
CSK’s 178. MI from 71/3 to 98/6 — the chase is slipping, with 2 Pathirana overs still left. Hardik scans the dugout: 1 impact slot remains.
The impact call belongs to the captain. In that second, he’s not looking at form — he’s looking at who’s ready.
His eyes stop on you — just for 1 second. Tilak beside you, silent. Tray in your hand — and 1 decision.
The call will come in 5 minutes — and whatever you’re doing right now is the data for it. What are you doing?

choices.s: Whether he calls you or not — the player who looks ready is the one who got ready early.

pass.title: IMPACT SUB — 14* (8)
pass.note: The captain lifted a hand: 'Kid. Pads.' A 2-over cameo — 2 boundaries off Pathirana, and in the last over they only needed 6 instead of 11. 14* off 8. Small number, big statement: when he looked, you were ready.

situations.title: Toofan
body: The morning after your debut, your phone's facedown and still blowing up — 348 notifications, 23 missed calls, 40,000 new followers overnight.
There's a storm with your name on it. Question is: do you live inside it, or rise above it.
situations.q: What do you even do with a hero-storm?

reader.text: 6:12. Phone face-down, still lighting up. 348 notifications. 4 interview requests, 1 brand DM. Coach sent just one thing: ‘Did you do recovery?’
Every third post is that same frame: Pathirana’s slower ball, your wait, the gap. The score isn’t the caption anymore — it’s the hashtag.
Every edit is the same 8 balls — from orange bib to Pathirana. ‘14 not out’ is small, the clip is huge. ‘SUPER SUB’ is trending.
In the middle of the scroll, one post quiets everything down — SKY’s.
Timeline chill. I’ve got the kid. You guys watch the match. 💙
Bro, half of those 23 missed calls were mine 😭 Don’t open Insta. Or do. You’re famous now and I’m in the comments fighting for your life.
There’s a storm with your name on it — do you stay inside it, or rise above it?

choices.t: Ride it — reels, interviews, all of it
choices.s: Momentum is currency. Today, you’ve got it.

situations.title: Hotel Gym. Alone.
body: Day 8, 5:52 a.m. Empty hotel gym, trigger movement gone. Rohit's door is on this floor — nobody knocked. Just Coach Sir on video call, and a slump that doesn't break on its own.
situations.q: A slump doesn’t break by itself. How do you break it?

reader.text: Day 8, 5:52 AM. Empty gym, Eliminator in 2 days. The orange bib feels normal now. The timeline doesn’t even say my name anymore — that hurts more than the trolling.
Day 8, 5:52 AM. Empty gym, Eliminator in 2 days. My name’s on the sheet — but my last 3 innings total? Barely an over’s worth. This silence is the loudest thing here.
Son, PR wrote the statement — but no video for 3 days, that part’s you. Don’t run. A slump starts in the mind, not the technique. Remember the cement wicket? We start with the grip.

Son, I heard — and you owned the mistake yourself. People will keep looking you in the eye, but form doesn’t come back out of respect. No video for 3 days. Remember the cement wicket? We start with the grip.
My trigger movement’s gone in the mirror; Rohit’s on this same floor — and still, no one knocked. In a 20-crore Mumbai, just 1 video call: how do you break a slump?

choices.t: Go back to basics with Coach
choices.s: Put the ego aside. Start with the grip — like when you were eleven.

dm.text: Got the video. Showed exactly what I thought — the backlift is fine, your base is shaky. You’re getting to the ball too early.
Tomorrow, 6 AM, we do drills on video call. 200 balls. Defence only. Not a single shot. Like we used to on the cement wicket.
And son — don’t look at the scorecard this week. Watch the ball. I’ll handle the rest of the world.

choices.s: Don’t wait on anybody. Your work, your story, your proof.

situations.title: Till the Last Ball
body: Eliminator. Chasing 168—you lose a wicket in the 11th, and the dugout points at you. Two overs later, the board is simple: 52 needed off 30. And the selectors are sitting in the stands.
situations.q: 52 off 30. How do you get there?

reader.text: Eliminator. Wankhede packed — 33,000 on their feet. Chasing 168, MI 89/4 — your cue.
2 weeks on the bench, one whiteboard number — now this walk. Recalls happen on 22 yards. The crowd remembers who you are.
At the toss, Hardik said it on camera: "The kid plays. My call." Now his word is in your bat.
(from the rope, carrying drinks) WIDE YORKER! First 3! Wait on it — deep point is open!
Rohit had said: "Either works, but decide." You picked your way — today it gets tested in front of 33,000.
52 off 30 — whole season on it, selectors in the stands, India’s list in 3 days. Hardik’s eyes say: we’re winning from here, only one question — how?

choices.s: Play the matchups. Respect the boring ball, punish the bad one. Till the last ball.

situations.title: The Verdict
body: Squad announcement—India A and T20I list, 6 PM. Right now it’s 3:47, your phone has 89 notifications, and Hardik is in the room where the list gets made. 2 hours. Where do you spend them?
situations.q: List drops at 6. Where are you till then?

reader.text: Day 11. India A and T20I list at 6. It's 3:47 right now, and my phone has 89 notifications. Hardik is in that room where the list gets made.
Yesterday's knock is in every highlight package. 'ELIMINATOR' is stuck to your name now.
Yesterday's loss is still sitting in my chest. But selectors notice fight even in a loss. Maybe.
Son. You were 11 when you said this day would come. The day's here. The rest is just formality.
Yesterday you won the match with your head, not your bat. Today we'll find out what the selectors saw on the broadcast — the bib, or the brain.
And that 'sources' story? The dressing room might forget. The selection room never does.
1 old thing is traveling with this list — that trade rumor. The selectors read that too.
BRO. 6 PM. I have 3 YouTube channels open and 1 astrology stream. I'M nervous and I'm not even on the list 😭
Before the list, one thing. What you learned this season won't show up on any list. That stays with you.
2 hours, 1 list — the longest wait of 16 years. Where are you spending it?

choices.t: Phone off — go to Coach's academy
choices.s: Hear the ending where it started. Cement wicket, old net.

dm.text: You here? Pad up. Your phone stays in my pocket — till 6, it's just throwdowns. Like when you were eleven.
Remember your first season ball? You were crying. I told you — forget the pain, never the fear. You didn't let yourself forget. Whatever happens today, that matters more than any list.
…Wait. Your phone's ringing in my pocket. 5:58. Unknown number — Mumbai code. …Son. Pick it up.

choices.s: Watch history happen. And let the first word be yours — whatever it is.
choices.postWhy: The list drops at 6. Whatever happens — the first word needs to be yours, not some headline's. {followers} followers are smashing refresh. Write the statement.

post.caption: Whatever 6 PM brings — I earned this season, I didn't beg for it. Mumbai bought me. Now cricket decides what they got. 💙 #TheVerdict

reactions.text: list loading… this kid's name was on every shortlist. now let's see what the committee saw.
Career comes before the statement. Both are still long.

A.caption: Bro turned his phone OFF on verdict day and went to the academy. I'm stressing for him instead. Update: some astrology stream says 'strong Jupiter'. 🙏

B.caption: Even today, the post came before the call. Times have changed. Same number, kid — call when the list drops.

narrLines.text: Wankhede. Blue kit. Your name on the squad list.
The dressing room hasn't bought the story yet.

narrChars:
Captain. Role clarity before ego.
He decides whether your confidence helps the team—or just your image.

The quiet one. One line that changes everything.
"That was a shot. That wasn’t a ball."

Freedom. But earned, not random.
"Read the field, then go crazy."

Six balls. No sledging. No smile.
The hardest mirror in the room.

Already trusts you. Watching you earn it.
"Anyone can get hype. Trust comes from doing it again and again."

rohit.unlocks: Backing from the seniors on the away leg ("Win the Room")
tips: Talk more about your process than the result—Rohit reads your thinking, not just the score.
Tell him straight and honestly how you think under pressure.
No shortcuts, no excuses—that’s how you lose his trust.

hardik.unlocks: Your name on every team sheet — and an India verdict at the end of the season
tips: A captain wants role clarity—know your role and own it.
Give direct answers; don’t turn it into a headline or drama.
Team first, ego second — act like it.

lowTrustFeed.hardik: Body language watch from MI training: the captain looked colder than usual around the new kid today. The talent's there, but the question of role discipline is still open.
lowTrustFeed.rohit: Quiet Rohit moment caught at nets. No public drama, but the senior didn’t look fully sold on the youngster today.
lowTrustFeed.surya: Usually Surya keeps every session light. Today the vibe around the new kid felt a little off. Paltan noticed.
lowTrustFeed.bumrah: Bumrah rarely reacts, which is exactly why today stood out. The technical chat with the youngster looked short and serious.
lowTrustFeed.tilak: Young table update: the friendly energy around the new MI kid looks a little complicated now. Competition is normal. Distance is new.
lowTrustFeed.mahela: Selection watch: MI staff still rate the talent, but trust in the youngster’s role still looks like a work in progress.
lowTrustFeed.coach: Old coach, new pressure. People close to the youngster feel the IPL noise is starting to change how he listens.
lowTrustFeed.friend: Off-field watch: childhood friends don’t always slide easily into sudden IPL life. Something feels a little distant around the new kid.

indiaCall.sub: Unknown number. Then Hardik's on-record line: "I put your name forward. The rest, you wrote yourself." T20I squad — the runs were there, and the room was yours too.

captainsBet.sub: India A tour — the captain’s backed pick. "The numbers are only halfway there. But I’m all in." Now it’s not about earning that trust — it’s about living up to it.

statsMachine.sub: India A — the numbers opened a door no one opened for you. The corridor was empty. Only Bumrah gave a nod. The scorecard made the case, because no one else did.

notYet.sub: The list dropped. Your name didn’t. No call either. But at 16, "not yet" doesn’t mean "never" — this story isn’t over, it just hasn’t happened yet.

dmHooks.naman: One slot, two people. Weird, right? Anyway — wanna hit nets together tomorrow?
dmHooks.mahela: Selection is a sheet of numbers and one question: can I trust the role? Keep both in order.
dmHooks.hardik: Wanted to talk about the role. Meet me after practice.
dmHooks.rohit: I’m watching you. Ask if something’s not clicking.
dmHooks.surya: Hey champ! Settling in a little? First week’s always tough.
dmHooks.tilak: Good session. Wanted to ask one thing.
dmHooks.coach: Call when you’re free, beta. Not urgent, important.
dmHooks.friend: BRO PICK UP THE PHONE. I have 47 things to tell you.

hardik: Stay locked in on your role.
surya: Come to nets tomorrow, I’ll show you something.
bumrah: Still late on the slower one.
friend: I showed everyone. You're famous now. Terrifying.
